question: What happens when several agents work the same backlog in parallel?

tasqClaimBoundary.shape: Tasq Local and self-hosted Tasq Server

sources.title: Orchestrate teams of Claude Code sessions
Get started with Copilot agents on GitHub

systems.name: Tasq Local + Server v0.4.2
systems.coordinationUnit: A commitment in one user-owned local ledger, separate from its temporary claim and each execution attempt.
systems.parallelBehavior: A live expiring claim hides the commitment from another actor's default next-work selection; expiry permits a higher-fence reclaim without rewriting attempt history.
systems.collisionBoundary: Coordinates who may work the commitment. It does not create a Git worktree or merge code.
systems.completionBoundary: A successful runtime attempt does not complete the commitment; evidence and, when configured, an independent decision remain separate.
systems.scopeBoundary: Published Local coordinates CLI/MCP consumers sharing one user-owned ledger on one machine. The published self-hosted Server coordinates authenticated remote clients; managed Cloud is unavailable.

systems.name: Claude Code agent teams
systems.coordinationUnit: A team-local shared task list with pending, in-progress and completed states, dependencies, lead assignment and teammate self-claim.
systems.parallelBehavior: Task claiming uses file locking to prevent two teammates claiming the same task; completed dependencies unblock downstream tasks.
systems.collisionBoundary: Agent-team teammates are not worktree-isolated. Anthropic advises partitioning files because same-file edits can overwrite one another.
systems.completionBoundary: Hooks can block TaskCompleted, while the docs also list lagging task status as a current limitation.
systems.scopeBoundary: One experimental Claude Code team per lead session; the task/team files are stored locally and in-process teammates do not resume with /resume.

systems.name: GitHub Copilot agents
systems.coordinationUnit: An issue assignment or Agents-tab prompt starts an agent session; a coding session works toward a branch and pull request.
systems.parallelBehavior: GitHub documents multiple sessions running in parallel and the Copilot app can isolate sessions in separate worktrees or cloud sandboxes.
systems.collisionBoundary: Isolation protects working copies; GitHub review and merge gates reconcile proposed repository changes.
systems.completionBoundary: The documented handoff is a pull request reviewed by a human, with iteration through comments or further commits.
systems.scopeBoundary: Agent apps let third-party agents use the same issue, pull-request-comment and Agents UI entry points. The cited pages do not specify an expiring cross-agent claim/fence contract.

systems.name: GitHub Copilot CLI /fleet
systems.coordinationUnit: One parent request is decomposed into smaller tasks and delegated to subagents managed by the main Copilot agent.
systems.parallelBehavior: The orchestrator evaluates dependencies and runs suitable subtasks in parallel.
systems.collisionBoundary: The source describes parent-managed subagents rather than a neutral shared backlog used by independent runtimes.
systems.completionBoundary: The main agent manages the workflow and dependencies and integrates subagent results into the parent request.
systems.scopeBoundary: This is orchestration inside Copilot CLI, not a cross-vendor coordination protocol.

systems.name: OpenAI Codex app
systems.coordinationUnit: Agents run in separate threads organized by project, each with an inspectable diff.
systems.parallelBehavior: Built-in worktrees give parallel agents isolated copies of the same repository.
systems.collisionBoundary: Worktree isolation prevents agents touching the same checkout; a human reviews, checks out or continues each change set.
systems.completionBoundary: The cited product page documents diff review and local checkout, not a shared commitment/evidence decision state machine.
systems.scopeBoundary: The cited page documents multiple Codex agents, not a vendor-neutral backlog lease shared with other runtimes.

systems.name: Cursor Background Agents
systems.coordinationUnit: A prompt creates an asynchronous agent whose status can be viewed, followed up or taken over.
systems.parallelBehavior: Each agent clones the GitHub repository into an isolated Ubuntu machine and works on a separate branch.
systems.collisionBoundary: Separate machines and branches isolate execution; repository handoff happens through pushed changes.
systems.completionBoundary: The cited page documents status, follow-up and takeover, not an independent evidence-bound completion decision.
systems.scopeBoundary: The cited page does not document a shared claim/reclaim backlog contract across agents.

systems.name: MCP Tasks and A2A Tasks
systems.coordinationUnit: A receiver- or server-generated task ID tracks one asynchronous request execution and its status/result or artifacts.
systems.parallelBehavior: Clients can list, poll, stream or cancel multiple executions; the specifications define execution lifecycles and interrupted input states.
systems.collisionBoundary: The cited specifications do not define an exclusive claim over an external shared backlog item.
systems.completionBoundary: Their completed state means the protocol task execution completed; neither specification defines a separate organizational commitment decision.
systems.scopeBoundary: These are interoperability protocols for executions, not backlog products. This classification is an inference from their normative data models.

conclusion.claim: Tasq's narrow differentiation is a runtime-neutral durable commitment/claim/attempt/evidence boundary. It is not the existence of parallel agents, subagents, worktrees, issue assignment or asynchronous task IDs.
conclusion.limits: Claude Code already demonstrates atomic claiming inside one vendor team; GitHub already owns issue-to-agent-to-PR workflow; Codex and Cursor already isolate parallel code execution. Tasq Local remains same-machine, Tasq Server remains self-hosted, managed Cloud is unavailable, and neither shape replaces those execution or code-merge surfaces.
